parsed.explanation: Combined regime exposes an outed trans visitor to selective criminalisation (new penal code in force Jan 2026, pornography law up to 7 years, provincial same-sex offences and Aceh caning), state threat-framing in the Oct 2025 defence decree, Aug 2026 vigilante mob attacks on trans women tied to officials' rhetoric, venue police raids, and a disputed death-in-custody case involving a trans traveller with alleged beating and $100,000 extortion. No operative anti-discrimination protection is documented. Execution is not documented, and national prosecution is selective, keeping the rating above the 0.15 tier, but state-tolerated targeting and imprisonment/canings place it below 0.25.

entry_documents.exposure: Airport arrest of a foreign trans traveller documented; no documented rule on foreign passport markers/X or mismatch handling.
entry_documents.interaction: Document/presentation discovery at airport can trigger investigation, detention and custody exposure.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Death in custody of trans traveller; mother alleges beating and $100,000 release demand, police deny violence; Aceh caning for same-sex conduct; capital raids on trans women to rehabilitation centres documented for residents.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Not documented. No functioning remedy for detained visitors documented.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Arrest for morality/pornography or provincial offences can lead to detention, caning in Aceh, or custody harm.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: No bathroom, ward or facility-access rule for visitors documented; Aceh Islamic code applies caning including to a person with gender disorder per dossier.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Subnational religious codes and >400 local bylaws, fines on trans women in two cities, interact with national morality provisions; national police sometimes refuse local rules.

care_services.exposure: Not documented for visitor HRT, medication import or emergency care.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Oct 2025 presidential decree lists LGBTQ+ people as nonmilitary national-defence threats; officials' rhetoric tied to Aug 2026 mob attacks; psychiatric association pathologised trans identities in 2016 with government silence.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: 2009 police regulation and 2015 circular on minority protection/hate speech exist on paper; enforcement outcomes not documented.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: State threat-framing licenses vigilante and police action; paper protections do not offset documented raids and rhetoric.

minors_guardians.exposure: Not documented. No age-dependent rule for trans minors or travelling guardians in dossier.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Aug 2026 vigilante mobs attacking trans women, described as escalating and tied to official framing; venue raid arresting 75 people at a villa in June 2025.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Not documented as effective for trans victims; no prosecution of attackers documented.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: State rhetoric plus selective enforcement creates impunity environment for societal violence.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No anti-discrimination protections as of 2019; gay police officer fired after outing, lawsuit rejected on procedural grounds in 2019; theoretical constitutional guarantee not shown to operate.
remedies_unknowns.protection: National police sometimes refuse to enforce local anti-trans rules conflicting with national guarantees; one job offer rescinded after human-rights advice.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Partial, inconsistent recourse does not remedy criminalisation, caning, raids or mob violence.

anchor_checks.comparison: Lower severity than 0.15-A: here prosecution is selective, execution not credible and routine months-long pretrial beatings for presentation are not documented nationally. Higher risk than 0.15-A only on state threat-framing and Aceh caning, but without its systematic arrest-to-beating pattern.

Similar to 0.25-C: birth-sex/religious custody harms, arrest leverage via morality laws, slow remedies and no execution. This case is lower because it adds documented mob attacks on trans women, a trans traveller death in custody, caning, and defence-decree threat framing.

Materially below 0.35-B: that anchor involves hours-long stops, fines and rarely imprisonment with no lethal threat. Here imprisonment up to 2 and 7 years, caning, venue mass arrests, and vigilante violence make consequences substantially more severe.

parsed.synthesis: National criminalisation and pornography/morality laws provide a police lever, Aceh and other provinces add caning and local fines, and the 2025 defence decree plus official rhetoric frame trans people as monitored threats, correlating with Aug 2026 mob attacks and venue raids. The disputed death-in-custody of a trans traveller with alleged extortion shows custody risk, though as a single disputed case it cannot alone prove systemic lethal custody. Paper minority-protection duties and occasional refusal to enforce local rules are unproven remedies. Overall: imprisonment, caning and state-tolerated violence are credible after outing; execution is not documented.
